claims.text: An equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy can be used as an interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
A HfNbTaTiZr interlayer will improve bond integrity under extreme thermal and oxidative conditions.
Vacuum sintering can produce nearly fully densified equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Water quenching HfNbTaTiZr produces a metastable single beta-BCC phase.
Slow cooling after sintering produces a multiphase HfNbTaTiZr structure.
HfNbTaTiZr can be provided with a silicide coating by pack cementation.
A silicide coating enhances the oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr.
Fusion-reactor plasma-facing components experience high temperatures, thermal cycling, and oxidizing environments.
HfNbTaTiZr has high yield strength attributable in part to interstitial oxygen strengthening.
The silicide coating forms self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 particles.
The HfNbTaTiZr microstructure can accommodate thermal stresses at a W/CuCrZr interface.
The HfNbTaTiZr interlayer mitigates the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
The interlayer provides a mechanically robust and oxidation-resistant barrier.
Mitigating thermal-expansion mismatch reduces interfacial cracking under cyclic thermal loads.
The proposed interlayer enhances interfacial shear strength under cyclic thermal loads.
Compared with conventional interlayers, HfNbTaTiZr will provide higher interfacial bond strength.
Compared with conventional interlayers, HfNbTaTiZr will produce fewer oxide-induced cracks and better thermal-cycling performance.
Current interlayer solutions commonly suffer bonding and oxidation problems that cause premature failure under extreme conditions.
The benefit is limited to temperatures at which the alloy phases remain stable and the silicide coating remains oxidation-resistant.
Scalability and long-term cyclic performance of this interlayer under fusion-reactor conditions remain unestablished.
